title: CSS custom property var() resolves at declaration scope, not usage scope
trigger: Component token (e.g. --button-bg: var(--color-primary)) defined in :root, but --color-primary overridden in [data-theme="dark"] on a descendant — token freezes to light value
principle: CSS custom property var() references resolve at the element where the referencing property is DECLARED, not where the property is USED. If --button-bg: var(--color-primary) is declared in :root, it freezes to :root's --color-primary value. Overriding --color-primary on a descendant (e.g. [data-theme="dark"]) does NOT re-resolve --button-bg inherited from :root. Fix: re-declare the component token block inside each theme selector so var() re-resolves with the theme-scoped color. Critical for Shadow DOM where data-theme lives on a descendant of :root inside the shadow tree.

cases.context: Shadow DOM popup: <html> has no data-theme, .cell-popup[data-theme="dark"] inside shadow has --color-primary: #60a5fa. Button uses var(--button-bg). --button-bg: var(--color-primary) declared only in :root → resolves to light #2563eb, button stays blue-light in dark mode.
Token generator script only emits component tokens in :root block, dark block only has color overrides — component tokens silently freeze to light values in dark mode

applyFor: Design token systems with component-level tokens referencing core color tokens (button-bg → color-primary)
Theme switching via [data-theme] attribute selector on a descendant of :root (Shadow DOM, iframe-injected roots)
CSS custom property cascades where a var() reference must track a theme-scoped override
Token generators / build scripts that emit :root + [data-theme] blocks — must emit component tokens in BOTH
Any case where inherited custom property seems to ignore a descendant override — check declaration scope vs usage scope
